_meta.title: MochaTrade Market Entry Readiness — Track 1 dataset

source_type_legend.verified_fact: a regulator/exchange/central-bank rule or figure, dated (Round 1 primary sources)
source_type_legend.calculated: the team's 1-5 rubric scorecard, built from verified facts against one fixed rubric
source_type_legend.route_requires_confirmation: flagged in Round 1 as not yet confirmed with MochaTrade's actual route
source_type_legend.assumption: stated assumption in Round 1 (e.g. partner availability, indicative FX)
source_type_legend.engine_reconstruction: NOT in the original deck — built for Round 2 to make the scoring/sequencing engine work end-to-end. Swap for real team judgment before the demo.

dimensions.label: Legality
dimensions.definition: Defensible route for the initial crypto-derivatives entry (US equities gated separately)

dimensions.label: Clarity
dimensions.definition: A usable licensing path exists today

rubric.note: Screening score identifies candidates. It does NOT set the entry sequence — adaptation cost and execution feasibility do (see sequencing_weights below). This is the deck's own 'SCORE ≠ SEQUENCE' finding (slide 6) and is the single most important thing this tool must preserve.

base.note: the exact weights printed on slide 4

regulation_heavy.note: slide 4 footnote says the top 3 were stress-tested under a 'regulation-heavy' weighting but doesn't print the numbers — this is a reconstruction. Replace with your working notes if you kept the real ones.

clear_threshold.note: Round 1 cleared the 3 markets scoring >=3.6 and screened out everything <=2.8; 3.0 is the midpoint used to decide whether a user-entered market clears. Not a deck number.

sequencing_weights.note: Lambdas are reconstructions. Since Round 2, adaptation_cost and execution_dependency are no longer typed in: they are derived from countable entry_facts (product rebuild, partner count, rail via partner, localisation, partner-fronted onboarding) taken from the Round 1 deep-dive text. See src/engine/sequencing.ts:deriveSequencingInputs().

markets.name: Brazil
markets.market_signal: B3 dated futures · 148M+ Pix users · SPSAV regime live

deep_dive.qualifies_reason: Largest commercial base on the shortlist — 148M+ Pix users; VASP regime now live.
deep_dive.crypto_route: BCB Res. 519-521/2025 create the SPSAV licence; crypto futures trade on B3 via a licensed intermediary — dated contracts, not perpetuals.
deep_dive.equities_route: CVM-regulated; local introducing-broker model has precedent. MochaTrade's route requires confirmation.
deep_dive.required_product_changes: Rebuild perpetuals as dated futures; Add Pix funding and withdrawal; Identify wallet owners on self-custody transfers; CPF-based KYC with COAF suspicious-activity reporting.
deep_dive.kyc_aml: BCB Res. 519-521/2025 put SPSAVs under Brazil's AML/CFT regime (COAF reporting); Res. 521 requires wallet-owner identification on self-custody transfers and pulls crypto flows into FX reporting. CPF-based KYC; COAF suspicious-activity reporting via the SPSAV partner or own licence.
deep_dive.capital_and_licensing: Partner with, or register as, a BCB-authorised SPSAV (own licence: BCB capital tiers apply). Filing window for existing operators closes 30 Oct 2026.
deep_dive.commercial_adoption: Pix at national scale; dated futures change the perpetuals UX — validate demand before full rollout.

sequence.label: Commercial scale
sequence.rationale: Largest base on the shortlist (148M+ Pix users) — worth the rebuild, so filing starts while Dubai is in build.
sequence.if_delayed: Hold at US equities until B3 access and product classification are confirmed.

markets.adaptation_execution_rationale: Medium adaptation cost: full product rebuild (perpetuals -> dated futures) but a well-precedented introducing-broker/SPSAV route, no new local exchange partner beyond B3 access. (Derived from entry_facts — see evidence.)

entry_facts.evidence: Perpetuals must be rebuilt as dated futures (rebuild); Pix is a national rail, no payment partner; one BCB-authorised SPSAV partner plus B3 access; app remains MochaTrade-fronted.

markets.entry_approach: Partner with, or register as, a BCB-authorised SPSAV; trade dated futures (not perpetuals) on B3 through a licensed intermediary; fund via Pix.

markets.name: Dubai (UAE)

deep_dive.qualifies_reason: Only rulebook that names retail perpetuals explicitly; dollar-pegged AED, no capital controls.
deep_dive.crypto_route: VARA Exchange Services Rulebook, Part V (ETD, 31 Mar 2026): perpetuals permitted at <=5x retail leverage, 20% minimum margin, suitability checks.
deep_dive.equities_route: Outside VARA's remit — separate securities-brokerage licence (SCA or DFSA/DIFC). Route requires confirmation.
deep_dive.required_product_changes: Cap retail leverage at 5x (below current India multiples); Add suitability checks to onboarding; Add UAE sanctions screening and Travel Rule on top of the India KYC stack.
deep_dive.kyc_aml: VARA Compliance & Risk Management Rulebook: full CDD/KYC, sanctions screening and transaction monitoring before onboarding; Part V adds suitability / appropriateness checks for retail ETD; Travel Rule on VA transfers. Reuse India KYC stack, add UAE sanctions lists and suitability questionnaire.
deep_dive.capital_and_licensing: AED 800k+ base capital (approx. US$0.2M), plus VARA custody/overhead add-ons. ETD authorisation is sequential to the base licence.
deep_dive.commercial_adoption: Small market: proves product and compliance, not volume. The 5x cap means less revenue per user but a clearer legal route. Aani instant rail; demand is a hypothesis to test.

sequence.label: Product fit
sequence.rationale: Only market where retail perpetuals are explicitly legal — the cheapest proof the product works under regulation.

markets.adaptation_execution_rationale: Lowest adaptation cost and execution dependency: closest product fit (perpetuals already explicit), lowest capital, direct licence (no local partner required). (Derived from entry_facts — see evidence.)

entry_facts.evidence: Perpetuals already explicit in VARA Part V (only a 5x cap + suitability); Aani rail; direct VARA licence, no local partner; English-language market.

markets.entry_approach: Direct entry on an own VARA licence: perpetuals at ≤5x retail leverage under the Exchange Services Rulebook (Part V, ETD); US equities need a separate SCA / DFSA licence later.

markets.name: Indonesia
markets.market_signal: 22.9M accounts · perpetuals live via licensed traders

deep_dive.qualifies_reason: 22.9M crypto accounts (OJK, Jul 2026); perpetuals already live on CFX through licensed traders.
deep_dive.crypto_route: Partner with a licensed physical crypto trader (Pedagang / PAKD) routing derivatives through CFX under POJK 23/2025. Partner terms require confirmation.
deep_dive.equities_route: US-stock access has local precedent via licensed intermediaries; MochaTrade's route requires confirmation.
deep_dive.required_product_changes: Switch to partner-fronted onboarding (cannot operate as a single app); Move settlement from UPI to QRIS / BI-FAST via a licensed payment partner; Define partner-owned KYC (NIK / e-KTP) and PPATK reporting in the partner contract.
deep_dive.kyc_aml: OJK/PPATK AML-CFT rules apply through the licensed Pedagang / PAKD: KYC is partner-fronted (NIK / e-KTP), MochaTrade does not hold the customer relationship; PPATK reporting and Travel Rule sit with the partner. Contract must define which party owns KYC records and STR filing.
deep_dive.capital_and_licensing: Own Pedagang licence needs Rp100bn minimum capital (exchange tier up to Rp1tn) — deferred; enter partner-led.
deep_dive.commercial_adoption: Large regulated ecosystem — Rp3.41tn monthly derivatives value (OJK, Jul 2026) — but the highest localisation burden.

sequence.label: Localisation
sequence.rationale: Strong demand (22.9M accounts) but two partners, new rails, new language — highest execution dependency.

markets.adaptation_execution_rationale: Highest adaptation cost and execution dependency: not a single-app model, needs partner-fronted onboarding plus a new payment rail (QRIS/BI-FAST) and new language. (Derived from entry_facts — see evidence.)

entry_facts.evidence: Cannot operate as a single app (rebuild); settlement via a licensed payment partner on QRIS/BI-FAST; two partners (Pedagang/PAKD + payment); new language; partner-fronted onboarding.

markets.entry_approach: Partner-led entry: a licensed Pedagang / PAKD routes derivatives through CFX under POJK 23/2025; settlement on QRIS / BI-FAST via a payment partner; own licence deferred.

markets.name: Philippines
markets.market_signal: BSP moratorium · SEC route · Php100M capital
markets.screened_out_reason: BSP moratorium on new virtual-asset-service-provider licences plus a Php100M capital bar keep legality and licence scores low despite real demand.

markets.name: Nigeria
markets.market_signal: Draft SEC rules · resident CEO · N2B capital
markets.screened_out_reason: Rules are still in draft, require a resident CEO and N2B capital — clarity and FX/custody too weak to clear.

markets.name: Pakistan
markets.market_signal: Licensing opened Aug 2026 · untested · rupee-only accounts
markets.screened_out_reason: Licensing regime opened only in Aug 2026 and is untested; rupee-only accounts add FX friction.

markets.name: Thailand
markets.screened_out_reason: The relevant access route is still a proposal (Aug 2026 SEC consultation), not a rule teams can file against.

markets.name: South Africa
markets.market_signal: 310 CASPs licensed · draft rule blocks self-custody transfers
markets.screened_out_reason: A draft Capital Flow Management Regulation would block self-custody inflows outright — the lowest FX/custody score on the board.

markets.name: Vietnam
markets.screened_out_reason: Ranks #4 globally in crypto adoption but the pilot needs ~US$380M capital and caps foreign ownership at 49% — legality and licence both fail.

sequencing_derivation.note: Each input is a yes/no or a count read directly from the Round 1 deep dive, so the sequence is explained by facts rather than by a tuned number. With the deck's facts this reproduces Dubai 1 / Brazil 3 / Indonesia 4 (adaptation) and 1 / 2 / 5 (execution).
